title: Ukraine Puts Putin’s Playbook to the Test

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访一些商界、政界和文化界最有影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订户，您可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望大家能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: To the outside world, Russia's relentless bombardment of Ukraine looks indiscriminate and improvised.
sentences.zh: 对于外界而言，俄罗斯对乌克兰的不间断轰炸看起来是无差别且即兴的。

sentences.en: In fact, it's part of a strategic playbook that Russia first devised 30 years ago in a different war.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是俄罗斯 30 年前在另一场战争中首次制定的一套战略剧本的一部分。

sentences.en: My colleague, Carlotta Gall, covered that war and explains why the Russian playbook used back then is essential to understanding what happens next in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我的同事卡洛塔·加尔报道过那场战争，她将解释为什么当年使用的俄罗斯剧本对于理解乌克兰接下来的局势至关重要。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 3 月 24 日，星期四。

sentences.en: Carlotta, you're in Kyiv.
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，你在基辅。

sentences.en: And the last time I saw you, I had come to your apartment and brought you takeout pizzas.
sentences.zh: 我上次见你时，曾去过你的公寓并给你带了外卖披萨。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was great.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: And then you had to rush back before the curfew.
sentences.zh: 然后你不得不在宵禁前匆忙赶回去。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we were sitting at the table and talking.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时坐在桌子旁聊天。

sentences.en: And I remember telling you that at the very beginning of the war, everybody, myself included, thought that the war would be quick, that the
sentences.zh: 我记得我跟你说过，在战争刚开始时，所有人都认为——包括我在内——战争会很快结束，

sentences.en: mighty Russian military would roll in and take the country in a week or even a weekend.
sentences.zh: 强大的俄罗斯军队会席卷而来，在一周甚至一个周末内攻占这个国家。

sentences.en: And I remember you telling me that you never believed that.
sentences.zh: 我记得你当时告诉我，你从来不这么认为。

sentences.en: And when I asked you why you gave me an answer, I kept thinking about.
sentences.zh: 当我问你为什么时，你给我的回答让我一直挂在心上。

sentences.en: Do you remember what you said?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你当时说什么吗？

sentences.en: I think I said that I thought the Ukrainians would fight.
sentences.zh: 我想我说过，我认为乌克兰人会抵抗。

sentences.en: But I also, I think, said, reminds me of Chechnya 30 years ago, nearly 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得，这让我想起 30 年前的车臣，差不多 30 年前。

sentences.en: And as you know, I covered the wars in
sentences.zh: 如你所知，我曾深入报道过车臣

sentences.en: Chechnya intensively.
sentences.zh: 那几场战争。

sentences.en: In fact, I was the foreign journalist who spent the most time down there in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我是 90 年代初在当地待的时间最久的外国记者。

sentences.en: And I saw it firsthand, the Russians crushing a people who were trying to stand up and be independent.
sentences.zh: 我亲眼目睹了俄罗斯人镇压一个挺身而出争取独立的人民。

sentences.en: And of course, it was a formative experience for me as a young journalist, but it stuck with me ever since.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对我作为一个年轻记者是一次决定性的经历，但它从那以后一直留在我的记忆中。

sentences.en: And I have this great feeling of recognition and familiarity already.
sentences.zh: 这种强烈的熟悉感和似曾相识的感觉再次涌上心头。

sentences.en: The sounds are some of the same, the bombs that are dropping.
sentences.zh: 声音有些是一样的，落下的炸弹也是。

sentences.en: But also this terrible feeling of dread of what this is going to turn out to be.
sentences.zh: 但同时也有着一种可怕的恐惧感，担心这一切最终会变成什么样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You said that the most important point of reference for understanding what's happening in
sentences.zh: 你说过，理解当今乌克兰正在发生的事情的最重要参考点，

sentences.en: Ukraine today is understanding what happened in Chechnya in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 是理解 20 世纪 90 年代在车臣发生的事情。

sentences.en: So bring us to that time and place, Carlotta.
sentences.zh: 那么，卡洛塔，带我们回到那个时间和地点吧。

sentences.en: What was the situation?
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是怎样的？

sentences.en: It all began with the breakup of the Soviet Union, you know, the end of communism.
sentences.zh: 这一切都始于苏联解体，也就是共产主义的终结。

sentences.en: And there was suddenly freedom, freedom of speech, movement, and so on.
sentences.zh: 突然之间有了自由，言论自由、迁徙自由等等。

sentences.en: And a lot of the former republics of the Soviet Union became independent.
sentences.zh: 苏联的许多前加盟共和国都独立了。

sentences.en: And then this little territory, which was still part of Russian Federation, but it's a sort of, it's its own region,
sentences.zh: 然后这个小领土，虽然当时仍然是俄罗斯联邦的一部分，但它某种程度上是一个独立的地区，

sentences.en: Chechnya, declared independence.
sentences.zh: 车臣，宣布独立。

sentences.en: There are only one million.
sentences.zh: 那里只有一百万人。

sentences.en: They're living in this mountainous area in the North Caucasus, Muslim.
sentences.zh: 他们生活在北高加索的这个山区，是穆斯林。

sentences.en: They'd been deported en masse by Stalin in the 40s.
sentences.zh: 他们在 40 年代被斯大林集体流放过。

sentences.en: So they had a lot of grudges, a lot of sort of tribal solidarity.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有很多怨恨，也有很多类似部族的团结。

sentences.en: And they decided they wanted, if not independence, autonomy, some sort of self-determination.
sentences.zh: 他们决定，即使不是完全独立，也要争取自治，某种形式的自决。

sentences.en: And so Chechnya declared independence and they started arming and training an army.
sentences.zh: 于是车臣宣布独立，并开始组建和训练军队。

sentences.en: And that's when I think Russia and the
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我认为俄罗斯和

sentences.en: Moscow authorities decided they had to act.
sentences.zh: 莫斯科当局决定他们必须采取行动。

sentences.en: And so they started preparing, looked like, to take back control.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始筹备，看起来是要夺回控制权。

sentences.en: And as tensions rose, I went into Grozny, which was the capital of Chechnya, and, you know, booked a hotel.
sentences.zh: 随着紧张局势升级，我进入了车臣首都格罗兹尼，你知道的，订了一家酒店。

sentences.en: And so I was there in December 1994, just as it was all building up.
sentences.zh: 所以我身在其中，那是 1994 年 12 月，局势正一步步升级。

sentences.en: We could feel there was an intensification.
sentences.zh: 我们能感觉到局势在加剧。

sentences.en: You could tell that the troops were getting closer and gathering, building up around the city.
sentences.zh: 你能看出军队正在靠近并集结，在城市周围集结。

sentences.en: There were reports that there was going to be final assault.
sentences.zh: 有报道称将会有最后总攻。

sentences.en: And then it came on New Year's Eve.
sentences.zh: 然后它在除夕夜降临了。

sentences.en: Russian tanks entered Grozny Saturday and began firing.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯坦克周六进入格罗兹尼并开始开火。

sentences.en: What happened was just so extraordinary that no one could have foreseen.
sentences.zh: 发生的这一切是如此非同寻常，以至于没有人能预料到。

sentences.en: The Russians, you know, did their operation.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人，你知道的，开展了他们的行动。

sentences.en: They bombed from the air and then they set off in columns, armoured vehicles and tanks, into the city.
sentences.zh: 他们从空中轰炸，然后成纵队出动，装甲车和坦克开进城市。

sentences.en: Their intention, obviously, was to go to the presidential palace and unseat the then president of the Chechen Republic and seize control.
sentences.zh: 他们的意图显然是直奔总统府，罢免当时的车臣共和国总统并夺取控制权。

sentences.en: It's approaching midday in Grozny, and this is the very centre of the city.
sentences.zh: 格罗兹尼正接近中午，这里是市中心。

sentences.en: The presidential palace is behind me.
sentences.zh: 总统府就在我身后。

sentences.en: The Russians claim they control it.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人声称他们控制了它。

sentences.en: It's obviously not the case.
sentences.zh: 显然事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And they never made it.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没能抵达。

sentences.en: On the way in, especially one brigade coming from the north, they got ambushed by Chechen fighters who actually knew the city very well.
sentences.zh: 在进城的路上，尤其是从北方来的一支旅，遭到了对这座城市非常熟悉的车臣武装人员的伏击。

sentences.en: Most of them were on foot or on small, in small vehicles.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数是步行或乘坐小型车辆。

sentences.en: And they trapped and ambushed the Russian columns as they came in, bombing and firing these shoulder-held rocket launchers at the tanks.
sentences.zh: 当俄罗斯纵队开进来时，他们设法将其困住并伏击，用肩扛式火箭发射器轰炸和射击坦克。

sentences.en: We hear that there are hundreds of Russian dead and many, many tanks have been burned out.
sentences.zh: 我们听说有数百名俄军士兵死亡，许多许多坦克被烧毁。

sentences.en: The Chechens burned the tanks, then they hit all the vehicles in between.
sentences.zh: 车臣人烧毁了坦克，然后击中了中间的所有车辆。

sentences.en: They trapped them if they tried to get away down side streets and knocked them out.
sentences.zh: 如果他们试图从侧街逃跑，车臣人就会把他们截住并将其消灭。

sentences.en: There is what someone described as a tank graveyard, where boys...
sentences.zh: 正如某人所描述的那样，那里有一个坦克墓地，到处都是...

sentences.en: It was an absolute wipeout.
sentences.zh: 这是一场彻底的歼灭战。

sentences.en: Carlotta, why did the Russians fail that time in Chechnya?
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，俄罗斯人那次在车臣为什么会失败？

sentences.en: Why did they get stuck?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会陷入困境？

sentences.en: Well, that was interesting because it seemed they were very ill-prepared.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有意思，因为看起来他们准备严重不足。

sentences.en: You know, ever since
sentences.zh: 你知道，自从

sentences.en: World War II and defeating the Nazis, they had this great huge army of tanks and massed troops, and they thought they could just walk into Chechnya and take it over by morning.
sentences.zh: 二战并战胜纳粹以来，他们拥有庞大的坦克和密集部队大军，他们以为自己只要开进车臣，到早晨就能将其占领。

sentences.en: The president at the time, Boris Yeltsin, had intended to have a small victorious war to boost his ratings and to show a
sentences.zh: 当时的总统鲍里斯·叶利钦本打算打一场速战速决的战争，以提升支持率，

sentences.en: bit of strength and clear up a problem in the southern regions.
sentences.zh: 展现一点实力，并清理南部地区的一个问题。

sentences.en: And of course, they were suddenly faced with this massive defeat.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们突然面对的是这场惨败。

sentences.en: And then there was a couple of weeks where everything seemed stalled, everything was in a sort of stunned silence.
sentences.zh: 接着有几个星期的时间，一切似乎都陷入停滞，一切都处于一种震惊的沉默中。

sentences.en: But what in fact was happening was that the
sentences.zh: 但实际上发生的事情是，

sentences.en: Russians were manoeuvring around, and they started flanking the city, digging in with big guns and artillery.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人在调兵遣将，他们开始对城市进行两翼包抄，用大炮和火炮构筑阵地。

sentences.en: And I remember standing on the sort of northern reaches behind Russian lines then, and when, you know, a few weeks later, when they really started to basically bludgeon the city
sentences.zh: 我记得当时站在俄军阵地后方的北部边缘，几周后，当他们真正开始把这座城市

sentences.en: into submission.
sentences.zh: 彻底轰炸至屈服时。

sentences.en: The firepower, once it was all in position, was just unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 火力一旦全部到位，简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: You'd just hear these boom, boom, boom, these huge guns fired into the city, artillery and shells and aerial bombardment.
sentences.zh: 你只会听到轰、轰、轰的巨响，这些重炮向城市开火，火炮、炮弹和空中轰炸接踵而至。

sentences.en: Shells screamed into the city centre at a rate of up to 10 a minute.
sentences.zh: 炮弹呼啸着飞入市中心，频率高达每分钟 10 发。

sentences.en: They hit everything.
sentences.zh: 它们击中了所有东西。

sentences.en: I mean, everything.
sentences.zh: 我是说，所有的东西。

sentences.en: The presidential palace, of course, was in the central square, was a main target.
sentences.zh: 总统府当然在中央广场，是主要目标。

sentences.en: But, you know, there was the theatre opposite, the cultural centre, they all got smashed.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，对面的剧院、文化中心，全都被摧毁了。

sentences.en: And apartment buildings all down the central avenue was a beautiful tree-lined central avenue.
sentences.zh: 中央大街沿线的公寓楼是一条美丽的有树荫的中央大街。

sentences.en: Every building got smashed.
sentences.zh: 每一栋建筑都被砸毁了。

sentences.en: Weeks of continued bombing and shelling by the Russians have reduced much of this city to rubble.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人数周持续的轰炸和炮击将这座城市的很大一部分化为废墟。

sentences.en: This is a lesson the Chechens won't easily forget.
sentences.zh: 这是车臣人不会轻易忘记的教训。

sentences.en: And as it came closer, the shelling, the Chechen fighters would pull back because they just couldn't sustain the lines under such heavy firepower.
sentences.zh: 随着炮击越来越近，车臣战士会撤退，因为在如此猛烈的火力下，他们根本无法坚守防线。

sentences.en: And so for months we followed the march of this
sentences.zh: 因此，几个月来，我们目睹了这场

sentences.en: incredible onslaught of bombardment coming steadily towards the centre from the north.
sentences.zh: 排山倒海般的轰炸从北方稳步推进向市中心。

sentences.en: What did Grosny look like after these massive bombardments?
sentences.zh: 经历这些大规模轰炸后，格罗兹尼是什么样子的？

sentences.en: When you went around the city, walked around, what did you see?
sentences.zh: 当你在这个城市转悠、四处走动时，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: That was a lasting memory.
sentences.zh: 那是挥之不去的记忆。

sentences.en: I don't think I'll ever forget it.
sentences.zh: 我想我永远不会忘记。

sentences.en: There's something horrendous about when a city is bombed like that.
sentences.zh: 当一座城市遭到这样的轰炸时，有一种极其可怕的景象。

sentences.en: All the roads disappear because they're covered in debris.
sentences.zh: 所有的道路都消失了，因为它们被废墟覆盖了。

sentences.en: You end up climbing over things or driving through mud and dust and rubble.
sentences.zh: 你最终只能翻越各种障碍，或者在泥浆、尘土和瓦砾中艰难行车。

sentences.en: And then everything goes really black, filthy black from sort of, I suppose, the gunpowder and so on.
sentences.zh: 然后一切都变得漆黑，被火药味之类的东西熏得肮脏发黑。

sentences.en: So we'd go into the basements to see and you'd find a lot of people were hiding down in the basements.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会进入地下室查看，你会发现很多人都躲在地下室里。

sentences.en: And then the most gut-wrenching thing was just to see these apartment buildings shorn off.
sentences.zh: 然后最揪心的就是看到这些公寓楼被拦腰截断。

sentences.en: And so you'd look up and you'd see a couch hanging out the window or a picture on the wall, but all skewed and things tumbling out of apartment blocks.
sentences.zh: 你会抬头看到一张沙发挂在窗户外面，或者墙上挂着一幅画，但都倾斜着，东西从公寓里倾泻而出。

sentences.en: That was people's lives just cut in half and falling out the window.
sentences.zh: 那是人们的生活被生生切断并从窗户掉落。

sentences.en: It was just that, I remember, was always really shocking.
sentences.zh: 我记得，那总是让人感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: So how did this bombardment strategy work out for the Russians?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种轰炸战略对俄罗斯人来说结果如何？

sentences.en: Well, they took the city in the end.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们最终拿下了这座城市。

sentences.en: I mean, it was an almighty battle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一场极其惨烈的战斗。

sentences.en: It took about three months, but they did take it.
sentences.zh: 大约花了三个月时间，但他们确实拿下了。

sentences.en: They flattened it.
sentences.zh: 他们把它夷为平地。

sentences.en: And at some point, the Chechen fighters pulled back into the countryside and up into the hills.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，车臣武装人员撤回了农村和山丘上。

sentences.en: And the Russians established control over the city.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人确立了对这座城市的控制。

sentences.en: And then they started moving into the countryside to pursue the fighters.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始向乡村推进以追击武装人员。

sentences.en: And the war went on in the countryside and up into the hills and into the other cities and went on for most of that year.
sentences.zh: 战争在乡村、山丘和其它城市继续进行，并持续了那大部分时间。

sentences.en: And so by the end of 1995, the Russians had pretty well control of the whole territory.
sentences.zh: 因此到 1995 年底，俄罗斯人基本上控制了整个领土。

sentences.en: But the Chechens were still around and they were a guerrilla force and they were moving and mobile.
sentences.zh: 但车臣人依然存在，他们是一支游击队，并且机动灵活。

sentences.en: The predicament for the Russians is then they'd pretty well taken every part of the territory, but then they had to hold it.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人面临的困境是，他们基本上占领了每一片领土，但随后他们必须守住它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, taking control of a territory is one thing, but holding it, running it, is an entirely different set of challenges.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，控制一片领土是一回事，但守住它、管理它，则是完全不同的挑战。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And that was the most amazing moment for me to see in August of 96.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是 1996 年 8 月见证的超级震撼的时刻。

sentences.en: So 18 months after the war began, the Chechens came storming out of the mountains and seized control of Grozny.
sentences.zh: 战争开始 18 个月后，车臣人从山里冲出来，夺取了格罗兹尼的控制权。

sentences.en: And they surrounded and attacked every Russian position.
sentences.zh: 他们包围并攻击了每一个俄军据点。

sentences.en: And the Chechens blocked them, bombarded them.
sentences.zh: 车臣人封锁了他们并进行轰炸。

sentences.en: And they basically trapped the Russians in their own city and brought the Russian army to a standstill.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上将俄罗斯人困在他们自己的城市里，让俄军陷入瘫痪。

sentences.en: It was extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这太非同寻常了。

sentences.en: And eventually they negotiated a withdrawal and the
sentences.zh: 最终他们谈判达成撤军协议，

sentences.en: Russians pulled out.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人撤出了。

sentences.en: So how does Russia respond?
sentences.zh: 那么俄罗斯是如何回应的？

sentences.en: Well, Russia took time out to prepare, but they basically didn't give up the plan to return and take control of Chechnya.
sentences.zh: 嗯，俄罗斯花时间进行了整编，但他们基本上没有放弃返回并重新控制车臣的计划。

sentences.en: And we saw the rise of Vladimir Putin, who in 99 was deputy prime minister to Boris Yeltsin.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了弗拉基米尔·普京的崛起，他在 99 年担任鲍里斯·叶利钦的副总理。

sentences.en: And he started to get very involved.
sentences.zh: 他开始深度介入。

sentences.en: And he then made
sentences.zh: 然后他开始

sentences.en: Chechnya a key aim, I think, to establish power, to show his strength.
sentences.zh: 我认为，车臣是建立权力和展示其力量的一个关键目标。

sentences.en: He also brought a ruthlessness that went the whole way.
sentences.zh: 他还带来了一种毫不留情的铁腕作风。

sentences.en: He didn't stop, but didn't pull his punches.
sentences.zh: 他没有停手，也没有手软。

sentences.en: In Chechnya today, Russian rockets founded an oil refinery and ground troops advanced on the republic's capital, Grozny.
sentences.zh: 在当今的车臣，俄罗斯的火箭弹炸毁了一座炼油厂，地面部队向该共和国首都格罗兹尼推进。

sentences.en: He went back to war in Chechnya with a much better organized operational force.
sentences.zh: 他带着一支组织严密得多的作战部队重返车臣战场。

sentences.en: So he went in with a great deal of weaponry and forces to retake the territory.
sentences.zh: 因此，他投入了大量的武器和军队来夺回这片领土。

sentences.en: As Mr. Putin settles into his new office here in the Kremlin, he's already made it plain that the
sentences.zh: 当普京先生在克里姆林宫的新办公室安顿下来时，他已经明确表示

sentences.en: tactics being employed in Chechnya, which have caused such suffering to the civilians there, were entirely his own.
sentences.zh: 在车臣采取的战术给当地平民造成了巨大的苦难，而这些战术完全是他自己的主意。

sentences.en: But he brought another element, which introduced another chapter, as it were, to the Russian playbook, which is not just mass force, but also a political and even, I would say,
sentences.zh: 但他引入了另一个要素，可以说为俄罗斯的行事手册翻开了新的一篇，这不仅是使用大规模武力，还有政治上的，甚至可以说

sentences.en: an ideological approach to controlling the people.
sentences.zh: 一种控制人民的思想意识方法。

sentences.en: And Carlotta, what did this repression look like exactly in Chechnya, this new Putin chapter?
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，这种镇压在车臣具体是什么样的？普京的这个新篇章是怎样的？

sentences.en: Smoke rises from the ruins of a Chechen village.
sentences.zh: 浓烟从一个车臣村庄的废墟中升起。

sentences.en: More evidence of the unselective nature of Russian bombing.
sentences.zh: 这是俄罗斯狂轰滥炸不分目标性质的又一证据。

sentences.en: It was as sinister, perhaps, or even more than the bludgeoning with artillery and bombs, because it's back to almost Stalinist repression.
sentences.zh: 它可能和火炮及炸弹的猛烈轰击一样险恶，甚至有过之而无不及，因为它几乎回到了斯大林式的镇压。

sentences.en: Where the Russian army is accused by human rights organizations of gross violations, following the discovery of mass graves and the disappearance of dozens of Chechen men.
sentences.zh: 在发现乱葬岗和数十名车臣男子失踪后，俄罗斯军队被维权组织指控犯有严重侵权罪行。

sentences.en: Arrests, disappearances, executions, human rights violations.
sentences.zh: 逮捕、失踪、处决、侵犯人权。

sentences.en: It became to the point where Chechens, who are pretty fearless, brave people, who have a very strong culture and self-respect,
sentences.zh: 这发展到了一种地步，使那些相当无畏、勇敢、有着极强文化和自尊心的车臣人

sentences.en: became terrified to lift their heads, you know, or to go outside their houses.
sentences.zh: 变得惊恐万分，甚至不敢抬起头，你知道的，或者不敢走出家门。

sentences.en: So it became a really, really frightening regime of suppression and brutality.
sentences.zh: 因此，这成了一种非常、非常可怕的高压与残暴统治。

sentences.en: And it's still like that.
sentences.zh: 而且现在依然如此。

sentences.en: And it's now rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 而且它现在已经重建了。

sentences.en: So the city of Grozny now looks like a modern provincial town, but the people are shadows of their former selves.
sentences.zh: 所以格罗兹尼市现在看起来像一个现代的省会城市，但人们却成了昔日自己的影子。

sentences.en: It's very, very sad.
sentences.zh: 这非常、非常令人痛心。

sentences.en: What you saw there, Carlotta, you know, the playbook and its evolution with Putin,
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，你在那里看到的一切，你知道的，这本行事手册及其在普京手下的演变，

sentences.en: I guess I'm thinking to the outside world, it must have looked improvised and indiscriminate and kind of erratic.
sentences.zh: 我想在外界看来，这一定显得很临时、不加选择而且有点反复无常。

sentences.en: But it sounds like what you're saying is that in a lot of ways, it was really quite deliberate and intentional.
sentences.zh: 但听你的意思，在很多方面，它其实是相当蓄意和刻意的。

sentences.en: And in its own cruel way, it was effective.
sentences.zh: 用它残忍的方式来说，它确实是有效的。

sentences.en: It sounds like from what you're saying, this became Russia's template for taking over a place it wants to control.
sentences.zh: 听你这么说，这似乎成了俄罗斯接管其想要控制的地方的模板。

sentences.en: Yes, and I think it's a KGB template.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个克格勃的模板。

sentences.en: I don't think Putin necessarily invented it, but he employed it in sort of living memory and we saw how he did it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为普京必然是它的发明者，但他在我们活着记忆的范围内运用了它，我们看到了他是如何做到的。

sentences.en: And I think it's not erratic.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它并不是反复无常的。

sentences.en: I think it's super calculated.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是经过超级计算的。

sentences.en: It's ruthless, but it's effective from their point of view, which is have complete control and have no one challenging the power at the center.
sentences.zh: 从他们的角度来看，它是残酷的，但却是有效的，其目的是实现完全控制，不让任何人挑战中央权力。

sentences.en: That's what the Chechen, you know, war was about for Moscow.
sentences.zh: 这就是莫斯科发动车臣战争的意义所在。

sentences.en: So they didn't want any domino effect, you know, or any spreading democracy or movements for self-determination or independence.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们不希望产生任何多米诺骨牌效应，你知道的，或者任何民主的蔓延，或是争取自决或独立的运动。

sentences.en: And this is the playbook that we now seem to be seeing play out in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在似乎在乌克兰看到正在上演的行事手册。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一个专注于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里打碟时，你每天都要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在您喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Carlotta, you've been describing this Russian playbook for war and how it developed in Chechnya.
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，你一直在描述俄罗斯的战争行事手册以及它如何在车臣发展。

sentences.en: And I guess I've been thinking about how much it does feel like this is what we've been seeing in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我想我一直在想，这感觉多么像我们在乌克兰所看到的一切。

sentences.en: So walk us through that.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们详细讲讲吧。

sentences.en: Where are you seeing it most vividly?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里能最生动地看到这一点？

sentences.en: Well, I think you have to say first the burning tanks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想你首先得提到燃烧的坦克。

sentences.en: That's the extraordinary scene that I remember so vividly.
sentences.zh: 那是我至今记忆犹新的非凡场景。

sentences.en: But we've seen a couple of weeks ago this column that came down from the border trying to drive straight into Kiev and to take the city by force.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到几周前，这支从边境南下的车队试图直接开进基辅并通过武力攻占这座城市。

sentences.en: And the Ukrainians managed to ambush it on the way and stall it.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人设法在半路对其进行了伏击并将其遏制。

sentences.en: And not in just one place, but in several places.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅在一个地方，而是在好几个地方。

sentences.en: And we've seen them.
sentences.zh: 我们都看到了。

sentences.en: They're lying on the roads.
sentences.zh: 它们横亘在道路上。

sentences.en: They're burnt out.
sentences.zh: 它们被烧毁了。

sentences.en: Some of them still have Russian soldiers lying dead around them.
sentences.zh: 其中一些周围还躺着俄罗斯士兵的尸体。

sentences.en: An unbelievable image, which we saw all those years ago in Chechnya, that it happened almost the same again today.
sentences.zh: 这是一幅难以置信的画面，我们在多年前的车臣见过，而今天几乎一模一样地再次发生了。

sentences.en: And like in Chechnya, they took stock.
sentences.zh: 就像在车臣一样，他们进行了评估。

sentences.en: They regrouped.
sentences.zh: 他们重新集结。

sentences.en: It was a lull.
sentences.zh: 这是一个间歇期。

sentences.en: Then we understood they were moving out into the countryside, digging in.
sentences.zh: 然后我们了解到他们正在向乡间开进，构筑防御工事。

sentences.en: And then we saw this onslaught of artillery and firepower on the civilian areas of the city.
sentences.zh: 接着我们看到了对该市平民区的大规模炮火和火力猛攻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So these real kind of attacks on civilian targets that we've been seeing, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直看到的这些针对平民目标的真实袭击，对吧？

sentences.en: The mall in Kiev, the apartment buildings on the outskirts, the theater in Mariupol.
sentences.zh: 基辅的商场，郊区的公寓楼，马里乌波尔的剧院。

sentences.en: These are civilian targets and it looks similar.
sentences.zh: 这些都是平民目标，看起来很相似。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And they, you know, you don't know what they're thinking, whether they think there's really important people inside or it's to terrify the population.
sentences.zh: 而且你，你知道的，你不知道他们在想什么，是觉得里面有真正重要的人物，还是为了恐吓民众。

sentences.en: But it's certainly, you know, a signature of the Putin, I would say, wars that he has waged,
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是普京所发动的战争的一个标志，我想这么说，

sentences.en: which is show the brute force to show who is in charge and to absolutely subjugate a people.
sentences.zh: 那就是展示绝对的武力来表明谁说了算，并彻底征服一个民族。

sentences.en: And there's also a sign of the next level.
sentences.zh: 这也是迈向下一阶段的一个标志。

sentences.en: Tonight, as Russian air attacks ravage more cities, Ukrainian and U.S.
sentences.zh: 今晚，随着俄罗斯空袭摧毁了更多城市，乌克兰和美国

sentences.en: officials say Putin's playbook will likely increasingly include the systematic kidnapping of local leaders.
sentences.zh: 官员表示，普京的行事手册可能将越来越多地包括系统性绑架地方领导人。

sentences.en: There are several towns and cities that have been occupied by the Russians.
sentences.zh: 有几个城镇和城市已经被俄罗斯占领。

sentences.en: Ukrainian authorities say at least four mayors have already been captured.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰官方表示，至少已有四名市长被抓。

sentences.en: The Russians grabbed Melitopol's mayor, Ivan Fedorov.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人抓走了梅利托波尔市长伊万·费多罗夫。

sentences.en: And they took the mayor of Melitopol.
sentences.zh: 他们带走了梅利托波尔的市长。

sentences.en: Who officials say was whisked out of city hall, wearing a bag over his head.
sentences.zh: 官员称他被套着头袋从市政厅被带走。

sentences.en: He actually returned, but we don't know quite what went on when they took him away.
sentences.zh: 他实际上后来回来了，但我们不太清楚他们把他带走时发生了什么。

sentences.en: Ukraine's prosecutor general is accusing Russia of kidnapping a Ukrainian journalist who was covering the invasion.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰总检察长指控俄罗斯绑架了一名报道入侵的乌克兰记者。

sentences.en: We've had some journalists who've had to, one who, you know, disappeared and was detained.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些记者不得不经历这些，其中一人，你知道的，失踪并被拘留了。

sentences.en: Some others who've had to escape because they were being on a list to being wanted.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人因为上了通缉名单而不得不逃亡。

sentences.en: The two Associated Press journalists, in a new harrowing account, they described their escape.
sentences.zh: 两名美联社记者在一篇令人揪心的全新报道中，描述了他们的逃亡经历。

sentences.en: The Russians were hunting us.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人在搜捕我们。

sentences.en: They had a list of names, including ours, and they were closing in.
sentences.zh: 他们有一份包括我们在内的名单，并且正在逼近。

sentences.en: And then we've also seen this amazing demonstrations that have been going on in the city of Kherson, which is occupied by the Russians.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还看到了在被俄罗斯占领的赫尔松市发生的惊人示威活动。

sentences.en: Cameras captured the moment Russian troops fired into a crowd of demonstrators in Kyrgyzstan.
sentences.zh: 摄像机拍下了俄罗斯军队向吉尔吉斯斯坦的示威人群开枪的时刻。

sentences.en: And they've started to use tear gas and shoot at the protesters.
sentences.zh: 他们开始使用催泪瓦斯并向抗议者开枪。

sentences.en: So we're still in the early stages, but there's some very familiar tactics going on.
sentences.zh: 所以我们仍处于早期阶段，但正在发生一些非常熟悉的战术。

sentences.en: OK, so just as in Chechnya, the playbook evolves in the face of obstacles.
sentences.zh: 好的，就像在车臣一样，行事手册在遇到障碍时不断演变。

sentences.en: But I guess we also really have to wrestle with the fact that Ukraine, of course, is not Chechnya.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们也不得不面对这样一个事实：乌克兰当然不是车臣。

sentences.en: So I'm curious, how does this strategy play out in a different country with different circumstances and different people?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，这一战略在有着不同环境和不同人民的不同国家是如何展开的？

sentences.en: Well, that's what we're all watching for now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我们现在都在关注的。

sentences.en: And of course, it's only just playing out.
sentences.zh: 当然，这一切才刚刚展开。

sentences.en: But there's many differences.
sentences.zh: 但有许多不同之处。

sentences.en: Ukraine is a huge country.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰是一个巨大的国家。

sentences.en: It's 40 million.
sentences.zh: 它有4000万人口。

sentences.en: Chechnya was just 1 million.
sentences.zh: 车臣只有100万人口。

sentences.en: It's also an independent country, so it has its own army.
sentences.zh: 它也是一个独立的国家，因此它有自己的军队。

sentences.en: They've mobilized the entire male population as well.
sentences.zh: 他们还动员了全体男性人口。

sentences.en: The other thing that I think is really key for any guerrilla war, because that's probably what it's already evolving into,
sentences.zh: 我认为对任何游击战都至关重要的另一件事，因为这可能已经是它正在演变成的形态，

sentences.en: and that is having a border with a sympathetic country where they can get out for rest and recuperation, medical help, and then also they can bring in supplies.
sentences.zh: 那就是拥有一个与友好国家的边界，他们可以在那里进行休整、医疗救助，还可以运进补给。

sentences.en: And it has the recognition, Western recognition, and that results in they're getting military aid and support from Western countries,
sentences.zh: 它拥有国际承认，即西方的承认，这导致他们能够获得西方国家的军事援助和支持，

sentences.en: the whole sanctions regime, but really the moral support as well.
sentences.zh: 整个制裁体制，但实际上还有精神上的支持。

sentences.en: So that's huge.
sentences.zh: 所以这意义重大。

sentences.en: But they've also, I think, got Western advice on how to fight and how to defend the cities against the missiles and so on.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们还获得了西方关于如何作战以及如何保卫城市免受导弹袭击等方面的建议。

sentences.en: So Chechnya had none of that.
sentences.zh: 所以车臣没有这一切。

sentences.en: They were on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们只能靠自己。

sentences.en: They were almost landlocked.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎是内陆地区。

sentences.en: And they never had international recognition for their cause.
sentences.zh: 他们的事业从未获得国际承认。

sentences.en: They had sympathy in the media and in the UN, but they never had this sort of support.
sentences.zh: 他们在媒体和联合国得到了同情，但从未得到这种支持。

sentences.en: So Ukraine has some advantages.
sentences.zh: 所以乌克兰有一些优势。

sentences.en: And what's really interesting is the Ukrainians, they know intricately the Russian playbook.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，乌克兰人对俄罗斯的行事手册了如指掌。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what really strikes me, talking to the Ukrainians, is they have a deep understanding of Putin and of Russian power.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是让我震撼的地方，与乌克兰人交谈时，他们对普京和俄罗斯的权力有着深刻的理解。

sentences.en: And they have this expression, we've got to break his teeth, break the teeth of Putin, to really show him, you know, where the power is and force him out.
sentences.zh: 他们有这样一种说法：我们必须打掉他的牙齿，打掉普京的牙齿，真正向他展示权力在哪里，并把他赶出去。

sentences.en: And what does that look like right now in Ukraine, breaking the teeth?
sentences.zh: 目前在乌克兰，“打掉牙齿”具体是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, that's what's very interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: As we see the Russians start to move around the city of Kiev and to encircle and use this horrendous bludgeoning with artillery and air power,
sentences.zh: 当我们看到俄罗斯人开始在基辅市周围移动并进行包围，并使用火炮和空中力量进行可怕的猛烈轰炸时，

sentences.en: instead of waiting, the Ukrainians are taking the fight out to the Russians.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人没有坐等，而是主动出击迎战俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: They've just launched the second counterattack in a week against some of the Russian positions around the city and in other cities.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚在一周内对该市及其他城市周围的一些俄罗斯阵地发起了第二次反击。

sentences.en: Yes, they're doing it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们正在这么做。

sentences.en: And that is, it's a very important method of attack that you don't sit and wait for the onslaught.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的进攻方法，即你不能坐着等待猛攻。

sentences.en: You go out and you sally out and you take the fight to the aggressor.
sentences.zh: 你走出去，出击并向侵略者发起战斗。

sentences.en: Meaning go on the offensive.
sentences.zh: 意思是转入进攻。

sentences.en: Go on the offensive, yeah.
sentences.zh: 转入进攻，是的。

sentences.en: Don't just guard your capital, but you actually have to go out and defeat the Russian forces as they're gathering around,
sentences.zh: 不只是守卫你的首都，而是你实际上必须走出去，在俄罗斯军队集结、

sentences.en: as they're trying to dig in and start their, you know, assault on the city.
sentences.zh: 试图构筑工事并开始对城市进行进攻时击溃他们。

sentences.en: So that's what we've been seeing the last few days.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们过去几天所看到的。

sentences.en: It's not clear if the Ukrainians are being successful.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚乌克兰人是否取得了成功。

sentences.en: They're claiming some success, but it's a tough fight, of course.
sentences.zh: 他们声称取得了一些成功，但当然这是一场艰难的战斗。

sentences.en: It sounds like what the Chechens could never really accomplish and what the Ukrainians stand a better chance of accomplishing
sentences.zh: 听起来车臣人从未真正完成的事情，而乌克兰人更有可能完成的，

sentences.en: is really striking back against Russia and disrupting the playbook.
sentences.zh: 就是真正对俄罗斯进行反击并打乱其行事手册。

sentences.en: I mean, kind of rewriting it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有点像重写它。

sentences.en: Certainly that's their ambition.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是他们的雄心。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what they're talking about and they're saying they'll do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是他们一直在谈论并声称要做的事。

sentences.en: And they think they understand that this is necessary.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他们明白这是必要的。

sentences.en: The only way to do this is to take the fight and defeat Putin and his playbook.
sentences.zh: 唯一的办法就是迎战并击败普京及其行事手册。

sentences.en: It's very ambitious.
sentences.zh: 这非常宏大。

sentences.en: I have no idea if they're going to succeed, but they've certainly got the desire.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是否会成功，但他们绝对有这个愿望。

sentences.en: And certainly on the ground now they're fighting like mad.
sentences.zh: 而且现在在地面上，他们正在拼死抵抗。

sentences.en: And some of these experts who have been watching these wars, as long as I have, are talking about this.
sentences.zh: 一些像我一样长期关注这些战争的专家正在谈论这件事。

sentences.en: This could be the moment that Putin has overreached and gets his comeuppance.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是普京用力过猛并遭到报应的时刻。

sentences.en: We'll have to see.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待吧。

sentences.en: I think it could still be weeks and months of fighting, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为战斗可能还会持续几周甚至几个月。

sentences.en: But as you said, either way, win or lose, this strategy is going to have an extraordinary amount of misery in store for the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，无论如何，无论胜负，这种战略对乌克兰人来说都将意味着无尽的痛苦。

sentences.en: I mean, by design, it's patient, it's brutal, and it emphasizes destruction and repression.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从设计上讲，它是耐心的、残酷的，并且强调破坏和镇压。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a very dirty war as well.
sentences.zh: 是的，这也是一场非常肮脏的战争。

sentences.en: It's already brutal as we've seen.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，它已经很残酷了。

sentences.en: You know, the casualties are horrendous on both sides already.
sentences.zh: 你知道，双方的伤亡人数已经相当惊人了。

sentences.en: And, you know, one thing I've learned watching Putin is he doesn't care how many people die.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我从观察普京身上学到的一点是，他根本不在乎死多少人。

sentences.en: He doesn't care how much destruction.
sentences.zh: 他不在乎造成多少破坏。

sentences.en: In fact, he doesn't mind destroying and then leaving it destroyed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他并不介意先摧毁，然后任由其保持废墟状态。

sentences.en: Carlotta, that brings me to wondering about you and kind of how you're feeling right now in this moment.
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，这让我想知道你现在此时此刻的感受。

sentences.en: I mean, you're in Kiev.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你身在基辅。

sentences.en: Knowing what you do, based on your experience in Chechnya, you know what's coming for the people in Ukraine in some ways.
sentences.zh: 根据你在车臣的经验，结合你所了解的情况，你在某种程度上知道乌克兰人民将面临什么。

sentences.en: Because you've witnessed this Russian strategy firsthand.
sentences.zh: 因为你亲眼目睹了这种俄罗斯战略。

sentences.en: How does that feel?
sentences.zh: 那是一种什么感觉？

sentences.en: Yeah, you have this pit in your stomach the whole time, this sort of dread.
sentences.zh: 是的，你整个人都提心吊胆的，有一种挥之不去的恐惧。

sentences.en: The hardest thing is actually interviewing people here who won't leave the city because they want to stay at home and they don't want to go and they've got nowhere to go.
sentences.zh: 最难的是去采访这里那些不愿离开城市的人，因为他们想守在家里，不想走，而且也无处可去。

sentences.en: And I find in my questioning, I'm slightly wanting to shake them and say, don't you realize, you know, it's going to get worse.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在提问时，恨不得去摇醒他们，告诉他们，你们难道不明白吗，情况会变得更糟的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's a very, very grim feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这是一种非常非常严峻的感觉。

sentences.en: You can admire the beauty of Kiev as you drive around.
sentences.zh: 你开车四处转转时，可以欣赏到基辅的美丽。

sentences.en: But, yeah, there's this lurking, lurking dread in the back that won't go away.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，背后那种潜伏的、挥之不去的恐惧感始终挥之不去。

sentences.en: It's like you're cursed with the knowledge of the past that's telling us something about the future.
sentences.zh: 就像你被过去的见闻所诅咒，而这些见闻正向我们预示着未来。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: We should learn from our mistakes, shouldn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们应该从错误中吸取教训，不是吗？

sentences.en: We should learn what's come before.
sentences.zh: 我们应该了解过去发生的事。

sentences.en: I think the Ukrainians do know, you know, they've seen Chechnya.
sentences.zh: 我想乌克兰人确实知道，你看，他们见过车臣战争。

sentences.en: So, I think what's amazing is they're convinced that they've got to fight and do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得令人惊叹的是，他们坚信自己必须战斗并付诸行动。

sentences.en: Not only for them and their country, when they keep saying this to us, we're doing it for the rest of, you know, Eastern Europe and Europe and the free world.
sentences.zh: 不仅是为了他们自己和他们的国家，正如他们一直对我们所说的，我们也是为了东欧、欧洲以及自由世界的其余部分而战。

sentences.en: So, they're very, very convinced and that's extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们对此深信不疑，这太了不起了。

sentences.en: I mean, really admirably extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的令人钦佩地了不起。

sentences.en: Carlotta, thank you.
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，谢谢你。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 不用客气。

sentences.en: Good to talk.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你聊。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, Madeleine Albright, the first woman to serve as U.S.
sentences.zh: 周三，美国首位女国务卿马德琳·奥尔布赖特

sentences.en: Secretary of State, died of cancer at age 84.
sentences.zh: 因癌症逝世，享年84岁。

sentences.en: Albright was named by President Bill Clinton as America's top diplomat in 1997.
sentences.zh: 1997年，奥尔布赖特被克林顿总统任命为美国最高外交官。

sentences.en: She dealt with the war in the former Yugoslavia and promoted NATO expansion into former Soviet bloc countries in Eastern Europe.
sentences.zh: 她处理了前南斯拉夫战争，并推动北约向东欧前苏联集团国家扩张。

sentences.en: A Czech refugee who fled the Nazis and the communists, she had a moral clarity in a job that often favors real politic.
sentences.zh: 作为一名曾逃离纳粹和共产党统治的捷克难民，她在经常偏爱现实政治的工作中展现了清醒的道德观念。

sentences.en: In her last essay for The New York Times, she wrote that Vladimir Putin, whom she described as, quote, so cold as to be almost reptilian, was making a historic mistake in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 在她为《纽约时报》撰写的最后一篇专栏文章中，她写道，弗拉基米尔·普京——她形容他“冷血得近乎爬行动物”——在乌克兰犯下了历史性错误。

sentences.en: And the Biden administration made a formal determination that Russian troops have committed war crimes in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府正式认定俄罗斯军队在乌克兰犯下了战争罪。

sentences.en: Speaking on his way to Brussels for an emergency summit of NATO leaders,
sentences.zh: 在前往布鲁塞尔出席北约领导人紧急峰会的途中，

sentences.en: Secretary of State Antony Blinken said he would share the information with allies and partners.
sentences.zh: 国务卿安东尼·布林肯表示，他将与盟友和伙伴分享这一信息。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, NATO estimated that between 7,000 and 15,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in four weeks of war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，北约估计，在乌克兰四周的战争中，已有7,000至15,000名俄罗斯士兵阵亡。

sentences.en: A senior NATO official said the estimate was based on information from authorities in Ukraine and Russia and from intelligence gathered from public sources.
sentences.zh: 一位北约高级官员表示，该估计是基于乌克兰和俄罗斯当局的信息以及从公开渠道搜集的智能情报。

sentences.en: By way of comparison, Russia says it lost a total of 11,000 service members in nearly a decade of fighting in its war in Chechnya.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，俄罗斯称其在车臣战争近十年的战斗中总共损失了11,000名军人。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了大批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党陷入了一场激烈、混乱有时甚至惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，讲述了人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
